hypothesis: The neuron responds strongly to high-contrast, monochromatic vertical or radiating linear structures isolated against a flat, medium-gray background. The activating features are typically thin, elongated forms—such as spider legs, hanging cords, plant stems, vertical seams, or instrument hands—that are rendered in deep black or bright white, contrasting sharply with a neutral, desaturated gray backdrop. The neuron remains invariant to object identity (spanning biological forms like spiders and butterflies as well as man-made objects like bolo ties and flagpoles) and polarity (dark-on-light or light-on-dark), provided the scene maintains a strict grayscale palette and the foreground object is cleanly separated from the featureless surroundings. The activating feature typically occupies the central 30–70% of the image, often aligning with the vertical axis or extending diagonally from the center.

natural.description: A vertical close-up reveals the central components of a bolo tie set against a muted, medium-gray fabric background with a grainy texture. At the top, a circular silver-tone slide acts as the focal point, though its upper edge is truncated by the boundary. The slide features a textured, embossed center with an indistinct relief design, encircled by a raised rim with a rope-like, diagonally striated pattern. Two thick, matte black cords emerge from beneath the slide and hang vertically, running parallel with a narrow gap separating them. These cords appear to be made of a braided material and contrast sharply with the lighter background. Terminating each cord is a polished silver-metal aglet, cylindrical in shape and tapering slightly towards the bottom. The left aglet hangs lower, extending further down the frame, while the right aglet is positioned slightly higher. Both metal tips exhibit vertical highlights, indicating a smooth, reflective surface, and connect seamlessly to the black cords. Soft, diffuse shadows fall slightly to the right of the cords and metal pieces, suggesting a light source from the upper left.

In a black and white close-up, a garden spider is suspended centrally, facing upward with its legs arranged in four distinct pairings that create a prominent X-shape. The spider's abdomen is large and oval, featuring a complex pattern of dark transverse bands alternating with lighter, speckled areas, and distinct indentations along its dorsal surface. The smaller cephalothorax is lighter in tone, appearing fuzzy or textured. The legs are long and segmented, marked with high-contrast alternating dark and light bands; the two front pairs extend upwards and curve slightly inwards, nearly converging at the tips, while the two rear pairs stretch downwards and outwards, anchoring the spider. Running vertically behind the spider is a thick, zigzagging structure of bright white silk, a stabilimentum, which stands out sharply against the rest of the scene. Faint, thin lines of the surrounding orb web are visible but less distinct. The background consists of a blurry, out-of-focus texture of mottled grays and whites, suggesting vegetation or a rough surface, providing a neutral field that emphasizes the sharp details of the arachnid and the central silk structure.

A high-contrast, grayscale close-up reveals a spider viewed from above, oriented vertically with its abdomen positioned at the top and cephalothorax below. The abdomen is a large, oval structure featuring a distinct pattern: the upper section is striated with horizontal bands of light grey, while the lower majority is a deep, solid black containing four prominent, bright white spots arranged in a central cluster. The two upper spots in this cluster are larger and more intense than the two slightly smaller ones beneath them. Connected to the bottom of the abdomen is the smaller, shield-shaped cephalothorax, which appears silver-grey with a fuzzy, velvety texture. From this central junction, long, spindly legs radiate outwards; the visible upper legs extend diagonally toward the top corners and are mostly dark, while the lower legs extend diagonally downwards, displaying sharp, alternating bands of black and white segments. The background is a soft, out-of-focus mottling of dark greys, providing no distinct features, which pushes the sharp, textured details of the spider’s body and striped legs into the foreground. Lighting appears to strike from above, casting high highlights on the white abdominal markings and the silver hairs of the cephalothorax, emphasizing the arachnid's volume against the gloom.
